judgements.justification: The notes show answers fitted to each committee's questions, not conflicting numbers or accounts; nothing shows the two responses disagreed in substance.
Both committees judged novelty against the right prior work, Pi-Net; they weighed the same closeness differently, and no verdict rested on a wrong account of it.
B gave a spotlight on ratings 7, 8, 7, 6 with a single 8, and its meta-review 'gives no reason for a spotlight'.
A's critics objected to novelty over Pi-Net and the significance of gains, technical points from the same field, not framing from a neighbouring field.

B's Rugm (8) engaged with detailed requests and raised after the rebuttal, while A's only positive reviewer, La4a (7), wrote a two-hour generic review and never commented, so A's AC saw 'no one strongly in favor'.
A did not reject because promised fixes were too large; its core objection, novelty over Pi-Net, was conceded, not promised away.
Neither area chair cited an assessment outside the visible reviews.
Both committees judged the paper as a method paper by novelty and gains; neither applied a contribution-type standard the other did not.
A's low scores held on central points, novelty over Pi-Net and gains within the run-to-run spread; oDAB's misread FID was not its main point.
